exercises.instructionEn: Use the information from Ex. 16 to write the letter Paul wrote to a friend while he was in Madrid.
exercises.instructionUz: 16-mashqdagi ma'lumotdan foydalanib, Pol Madridda ekanida do'stiga yozgan xatni yozing.
exercises.explanationUz:
MANBA: 107-betdagi 16-mashq dialogi.

POL HAQIDA MA'LUM BO'LGAN NARSALAR:
  • Madridda
  • o'tgan dushanbadan beri shu yerda
  • do'sti Karlos bilan turadi
  • Prado muzeyiga borgan (o'tgan dushanba),
    u yerda go'zal kartinalar ko'rgan
  • Palacio Real'ga borgan (kecha),
    marosim xonalari ulug'vor edi
  • hali xarid qilgani bormagan
  • Rastro bozoriga borishni rejalashtirgan
  • paelya yeb ko'rgan ('Lhardy'
    restoranida, o'tgan kecha)
  • bugun kechqurun Carmen operasiga boradi


TO'LIQ NAMUNA XAT:

  ─────────────────────────────────────────
  Dear Tom,

  Greetings from Madrid! I'm having a
  wonderful time here. I'm staying with my
  friend Carlos and I've been here since last
  Monday.

  I've already visited a lot of places. I've
  been to the Prado Museum — I went there last
  Monday and I saw some beautiful paintings.
  I've also been to Palacio Real. I went there
  yesterday and the state rooms were
  magnificent. Last night I went to a
  restaurant called 'Lhardy' with some friends
  and I tried paella. The food was just
  delicious!

  I haven't been shopping yet, but I'm going
  to go to the Rastro flea market soon to buy
  some souvenirs. Tonight I'm going to the
  opera to see Carmen.

  Madrid is a fascinating city — you must
  visit it one day!

                            Best wishes,
                            Paul
  ─────────────────────────────────────────


TO'LIQ TARJIMASI:

  Hurmatli Tom,

  Madriddan salom! Bu yerda ajoyib vaqt
  o'tkazyapman. Do'stim Karlos bilan turibman
  va o'tgan dushanbadan beri shu yerdaman.

  Allaqachon ko'p joylarga bordim. Prado
  muzeyiga borganman — u yerga o'tgan dushanba
  kuni bordim va bir necha go'zal kartina
  ko'rdim. Palacio Real'ga ham borganman.
  U yerga kecha bordim, marosim xonalari
  ulug'vor edi. O'tgan kecha do'stlarim bilan
  'Lhardy' restoraniga borib, paelya yeb
  ko'rdim. Ovqat juda mazali edi!

  Hali xarid qilgani bormadim, lekin tez orada
  sovg'a olish uchun Rastro bozoriga boraman.
  Bugun kechqurun Carmen operasiga boraman.

  Madrid — maftunkor shahar, bir kun kelib
  albatta borishing kerak!

                    Eng yaxshi tilaklar bilan,
                    Pol
  ─────────────────────────────────────────


⚠ XATNING TUZILIShI — 105-BETDAGI JEKNING
XATI BILAN BIR XIL:

  1-xatboshi:  SALOM + qayerdaligi + kim
               bilan + qachondan beri
               (Present Perfect: 'I've been
                here SINCE ...')

  2-xatboshi:  QILGAN ishlar
               (Present Perfect → Past Simple
                naqshi)

  3-xatboshi:  QILMAGAN ishlar + REJALAR
               ('haven't ... YET' + 'going to')

  4-xatboshi:  BAHO + tavsiya
               ('a fascinating city —
                you must visit it')

  Yakun:       Best wishes, [ism]


⚠ ENG MUHIM NAQSh — HAR ISh IKKI ZAMONDA:

  'I've BEEN to the Prado Museum.'
     (Present Perfect — umumiy xabar)
  'I WENT there LAST MONDAY.'
     (Past Simple — aniq vaqt)

  'I've also BEEN to Palacio Real.'
  'I WENT there YESTERDAY.'

  Bu — Unit 15 ning oltin qoidasi.


KERAKLI IBORALAR:

  SALOM:
     'Greetings from [shahar]!'
     'I'm having a wonderful time.'

  QANChA VAQT:
     'I've been here SINCE last Monday.'
     'I've been here FOR a week.'

  QILGAN:
     'I've ALREADY visited ...'
     'I've also BEEN to ...'

  QILMAGAN:
     'I haven't ... YET.'

  REJA:
     'I'm GOING TO ...'
     'Tonight I'M GOING to ...'

  YAKUN:
     '... is a fascinating city —
      you must visit it one day!'
     'Best wishes,'


DIQQAT — 'A RESTAURANT CALLED 'LHARDY'':
  'a restaurant CALLED Lhardy' = 'Lhardy'
  deb ataladigan restoran

  'called' — nom berish uchun.


DIQQAT — XATDA OLMOSh:
  Dialogda Pol 'I' deb gapiradi, xat ham
  Poldan yozilgani uchun 'I' saqlanadi.

  (105-betdagi 4b-mashqda esa savolga javob
   berilgani uchun 'he' ga o'zgargan edi.)


YANGI SO'ZLAR:
  a project    = loyiha
  while        = ... paytda
  called       = ... deb ataladigan

sections.title: Reading & Listening — Tipping in America
sections.titleUz: O'qish va tinglash — Amerikada choychaqa berish

exercises.explanationUz:
MATNNING TO'LIQ NUSXASI:

  TIPPING IN AMERICA

  Americans take tipping more seriously than
  any other nationality, and of all Americans,
  no one takes tipping as seriously as hotel
  bellboys do.

  Tip your bellboy generously, and you'll have
  the perfect holiday. Don't tip him, and
  you'll have the worst holiday of your life!

  Guests who don't tip well at hotels often
  find that the heating in their room
  'accidentally' stops working in the middle of
  winter, or that they receive strange phone
  calls in the middle of the night. Sometimes
  the keys for their room 'disappear' and it
  seems that no one can find the spare keys.

  It's a good idea to tip a bellboy at least $5
  and, for tips of $20 or more, your bellboy
  will be your friend forever. So, anyone who
  is planning to stay in an American hotel
  should remember — bellboys can make sure you
  have the holiday of your dreams ... or they
  can make your visit a nightmare!


TO'LIQ TARJIMASI:

  AMERIKADA ChOYChAQA BERISh

  Amerikaliklar choychaqa berishga boshqa
  har qanday millatdan ko'ra jiddiyroq
  qaraydi, va barcha amerikaliklar orasida
  hech kim mehmonxona xizmatchilaridek
  jiddiy qaramaydi.

  Xizmatchiga saxiylik bilan choychaqa
  bering — mukammal ta'til o'tkazasiz.
  Bermang — umringizdagi eng yomon ta'til
  bo'ladi!

  Mehmonxonada yaxshi choychaqa bermaydigan
  mehmonlar ko'pincha xonasidagi isitish
  qishning o'rtasida 'tasodifan' ishlashdan
  to'xtaganini yoki tunning yarmida g'alati
  telefon qo'ng'iroqlari kelayotganini
  sezishadi. Ba'zan xona kalitlari
  'yo'qoladi' va hech kim zaxira kalitlarni
  topa olmaydiganday tuyuladi.

  Xizmatchiga kamida 5 dollar berish yaxshi
  fikr, 20 dollar va undan ko'p bo'lsa,
  xizmatchi umrbod do'stingizga aylanadi.
  Shunday ekan, Amerika mehmonxonasida
  turishni rejalashtirayotgan har kim shuni
  esda tutsin — xizmatchilar sizga orzudagi
  ta'tilni ham ta'minlay oladi... yoki
  tashrifingizni dahshatli tushga aylantira
  oladi!


QALIN HARFDAGI SO'ZLAR — TUShUNTIRISh
(17b-mashq shuni so'raydi):

  TIPPING = choychaqa berish
     'a tip' = choychaqa (xizmat uchun
     qo'shimcha pul)
     'to tip somebody' = choychaqa bermoq

  NATIONALITY = millat
     'What nationality are you?'
     = Millatingiz nima?

  GENEROUSLY = saxiylik bilan
     'generous' = saxiy
     'generosity' = saxiylik

  GUESTS = mehmonlar
     Mehmonxonada — turgan odamlar.

  HEATING = isitish (tizimi)
     'to heat' = isitmoq
     'a heater' = isitgich

  'ACCIDENTALLY' = tasodifan
     Qo'shtirnoq ichida, chunki ASLIDA
     tasodif emas — ataylab qilingan!

  RECEIVE = olmoq (qabul qilmoq)
     'receive a phone call' = qo'ng'iroq olmoq
     Yozilishi: rec-EI-ve (I dan oldin E)

  'DISAPPEAR' = yo'qolmoq
     dis + appear (appear = paydo bo'lmoq)
     Qo'shtirnoq ichida — o'z-o'zidan
     yo'qolmagan!

  SPARE = zaxira, qo'shimcha
     'spare keys' = zaxira kalitlar
     'a spare room' = mehmon xonasi

  NIGHTMARE = dahshatli tush, kabus
     night + mare (qadimgi so'z)
     'to have a nightmare' = qo'rqinchli
     tush ko'rmoq


⚠ DIQQAT — QO'ShTIRNOQLARNING MA'NOSI:

  Matnda IKKI so'z qo'shtirnoq ichida:
     'accidentally'  va  'disappear'

  Bu — KINOYA. Yozuvchi aslida bunday
  emasligini bildiryapti:
     isitish 'tasodifan' to'xtamaydi —
     xizmatchi ataylab o'chirib qo'yadi;
     kalitlar 'yo'qolmaydi' — yashiriladi.

  Ingliz tilida qo'shtirnoq shu maqsadda
  ko'p ishlatiladi.


GRAMMATIK QURILMALAR:

  1) 'as ... as' — TENGLIK:
     'no one takes tipping AS SERIOUSLY AS
      hotel bellboys do'
     = hech kim xizmatchilarchalik jiddiy
       qaramaydi

  2) 'more ... than' — QIYOS:
     'Americans take tipping MORE SERIOUSLY
      THAN any other nationality'

  3) BUYRUQ + AND + natija:
     'TIP your bellboy generously, AND you'll
      have the perfect holiday.'
     'DON'T TIP him, AND you'll have the worst
      holiday.'

     DIQQAT: bu yerda 'and' — 'shunda'
     ma'nosida (Unit 14 dagi 'or' = 'aks
     holda' ning teskarisi).

  4) 'WHO' bilan ergash gap:
     'Guests WHO don't tip well ...'
     'anyone WHO is planning to stay ...'


YANGI SO'ZLAR:
  to tip / a tip = choychaqa bermoq / choychaqa
  seriously      = jiddiy
  a nationality  = millat
  a bellboy      = mehmonxona xizmatchisi
                   (yuk tashuvchi)
  generously     = saxiylik bilan
  perfect        = mukammal
  the worst      = eng yomon
  a guest        = mehmon
  heating        = isitish
  accidentally   = tasodifan
  in the middle of = ... o'rtasida
  to receive     = olmoq
  strange        = g'alati
  to disappear   = yo'qolmoq
  spare          = zaxira
  at least       = kamida
  forever        = umrbod
  to make sure   = ta'minlamoq, ishonch hosil
                   qilmoq
  a nightmare    = dahshatli tush, kabus

exercises.explanationUz:
DIQQAT — AUDIO ShART EMAS:
  Uchala javob 'TIPPING IN AMERICA' matnida
  SO'ZMA-SO'Z bor, va matn XUDDI ShU BETDA
  bosilgan!


BARCHA JAVOBLAR:
  1  AMERICANS
  2  BELLBOY
  3  $20


HAR BIRI — MATNDAN DALIL:

 1  'AMERICANS / Canadians take tipping more
     seriously than any other nationality.'

    MATNNING BIRINCHI GAPI:
    'AMERICANS take tipping more seriously
     than any other nationality.'
    → AMERICANS

    Matnda 'Canadians' (kanadaliklar) umuman
    tilga olinmaydi.

 2  'Tip your BELLBOY / travel agent
     generously, and you'll have the perfect
     holiday.'

    MATNDAN:
    'Tip your BELLBOY generously, and you'll
     have the perfect holiday.'
    → BELLBOY

    Matnda 'travel agent' (sayohat agenti)
    umuman yo'q.

 3  'For tips of $60 / $20 or more, your
     bellboy will be your friend forever.'

    MATNDAN:
    'for tips of $20 OR MORE, your bellboy
     will be your friend forever.'
    → $20


DIQQAT — MATNDAGI IKKI SUMMA:
  Matnda IKKI pul miqdori bor:
     'AT LEAST $5'      — eng kam miqdor
     '$20 OR MORE'      — do'st bo'lish uchun

  3-band 'friend forever' haqida, demak $20.
  ($5 — 17b ning 3-savolida so'raladi.)

  Kitob ataylab ikki summani bergan.


YANGI SO'ZLAR:
  a Canadian    = kanadalik
  a travel agent = sayohat agenti
  a bellboy     = mehmonxona xizmatchisi
  forever       = umrbod

exercises.instructionEn: Read the text below and choose the best answer to the questions that follow, then explain the words in bold.
exercises.instructionUz: Quyidagi matnni o'qing va savollarga eng to'g'ri javobni tanlang, so'ngra qalin harfdagi so'zlarni tushuntiring.
exercises.explanationUz:
BARCHA JAVOBLAR:
  1  C
  2  A
  3  C
  4  B


HAR BIRI — MATNDAN DALIL:

 1  'What happens to people who don't tip
     bellboys in the USA?'
    A They will have a great holiday.
    B The bellboys will like them.
    C They will have a very bad holiday.  ✓

    MATNDAN:
    'DON'T TIP HIM, and you'll have the WORST
     HOLIDAY OF YOUR LIFE!'

    A va B — matnga ZID.
    → C

 2  'Which of the following can happen to
     guests who don't tip well?'
    A Their heating goes off in the middle of
      winter.  ✓
    B They get more keys for their room.
    C They don't get any phone calls.

    MATNDAN:
    'the HEATING in their room "accidentally"
     STOPS WORKING in the MIDDLE OF WINTER'

    B NEGA XATO: matnda kalitlar KO'PAYMAYDI,
      balki 'DISAPPEAR' (yo'qoladi)!
    C NEGA XATO: matnda ular qo'ng'iroq
      OLADI ('they RECEIVE strange phone
      calls'), olmaydi emas!

    → A

 3  'It's a good idea to tip a bellboy at
     least ...'
    A $50.   B $15.   C $5.  ✓

    MATNDAN:
    'It's a good idea to tip a bellboy AT
     LEAST $5'

    → C
    (DIQQAT: $20 — boshqa summa, 'friend
     forever' uchun.)

 4  'Bellboys can make sure you have....'
    A a cheap or an expensive holiday.
    B a good or a bad holiday.  ✓
    C a clean or a dirty room.

    MATNNING OXIRGI GAPI:
    'bellboys can MAKE SURE you have the
     HOLIDAY OF YOUR DREAMS ... or they can
     make your visit a NIGHTMARE!'

    'holiday of your dreams' = yaxshi ta'til
    'nightmare' = yomon ta'til
    → B

    A NEGA XATO: matnda NARX haqida gap yo'q.
    C NEGA XATO: matnda TOZALIK haqida gap
      yo'q (isitish, kalit, qo'ng'iroq bor).


⚠ 2-SAVOL — ENG NOZIK:
  Uchala variant ham matndagi narsalarni
  tilga oladi (isitish, kalit, qo'ng'iroq),
  lekin IKKITASI TESKARI aytilgan:

     B  'get MORE keys'  ✗
        Matn: kalitlar 'DISAPPEAR'

     C  'DON'T get any phone calls'  ✗
        Matn: 'they RECEIVE strange phone
              calls'

  Faqat A matnga to'g'ri mos keladi.


QALIN HARFDAGI SO'ZLAR — TUShUNTIRISh:

  TIPPING     = choychaqa berish
  NATIONALITY = millat
  GENEROUSLY  = saxiylik bilan
  GUESTS      = mehmonlar
  HEATING     = isitish (tizimi)
  ACCIDENTALLY = tasodifan (kinoya bilan!)
  RECEIVE     = olmoq
  DISAPPEAR   = yo'qolmoq (kinoya bilan!)
  SPARE       = zaxira
  NIGHTMARE   = dahshatli tush, kabus


DIQQAT — 'HEATING GOES OFF':
  2-savolning A varianti 'goes off' deydi,
  matnda esa 'stops working'.

  'to go off' = o'chib qolmoq (isitish,
  chiroq haqida)
  'to stop working' = ishlashdan to'xtamoq

  Ikkalasi ham bir xil ma'no — kitob ataylab
  boshqa so'z bilan aytgan (o'quvchi
  MA'NONI tushunishi kerak, so'zni emas).


YANGI SO'ZLAR:
  to go off   = o'chib qolmoq
  cheap       = arzon
  expensive   = qimmat
  dirty       = iflos
  the following = quyidagi

items.answer: C  They will have a very bad holiday.
options: C  They will have a very bad holiday.
A  They will have a great holiday.
B  The bellboys will like them.
items.uz: AQShda xizmatchilarga choychaqa bermaydiganlarga nima bo'ladi? — Ular juda yomon ta'til o'tkazadi.
items.whyUz:
MATNDAN so'zma-so'z:
'DON'T TIP HIM, and you'll have the WORST
HOLIDAY OF YOUR LIFE!'

A va B — matnga ZID (aksincha, choychaqa
BERGANLAR yaxshi ta'til o'tkazadi).

items.textEn: 2  Which of the following can happen to guests who don't tip well?  A Their heating goes off in the middle of winter.  B They get more keys for their room.  C They don't get any phone calls.
items.answer: A  Their heating goes off in the middle of winter.
options: A  Their heating goes off in the middle of winter.
B  They get more keys for their room.
C  They don't get any phone calls.
items.uz: Yaxshi choychaqa bermaydigan mehmonlarga quyidagilardan qaysi biri bo'lishi mumkin? — Xonasidagi isitish qish o'rtasida o'chib qoladi.
items.whyUz:
MATNDAN:
'the HEATING in their room "accidentally"
STOPS WORKING in the MIDDLE OF WINTER'

⚠ ENG NOZIK SAVOL — B va C TESKARI aytilgan:

  B XATO: matnda kalitlar KO'PAYMAYDI, balki
     'DISAPPEAR' (yo'qoladi).
  C XATO: matnda ular qo'ng'iroq OLADI
     ('they RECEIVE strange phone calls'),
     olmaydi emas!

'to go off' = 'to stop working' (o'chib qolmoq).

items.textEn: 3  It's a good idea to tip a bellboy at least ...  A $50.  B $15.  C $5.
items.uz: Xizmatchiga kamida ... berish yaxshi fikr. — 5 dollar.
items.whyUz:
MATNDAN so'zma-so'z:
'It's a good idea to tip a bellboy AT LEAST
$5'

DIQQAT: matnda IKKI summa bor —
  $5  — eng kam miqdor (bu savol)
  $20 — 'friend forever' uchun (17a, 3-band)

$50 va $15 matnda umuman yo'q.

items.textEn: 4  Bellboys can make sure you have....  A a cheap or an expensive holiday.  B a good or a bad holiday.  C a clean or a dirty room.
items.answer: B  a good or a bad holiday.
options: B  a good or a bad holiday.
A  a cheap or an expensive holiday.
C  a clean or a dirty room.
items.uz: Xizmatchilar sizga ... ta'minlay oladi. — yaxshi yoki yomon ta'til.
items.whyUz:
MATNNING OXIRGI GAPI:
'bellboys can MAKE SURE you have the HOLIDAY
OF YOUR DREAMS ... or they can make your
visit a NIGHTMARE!'

'holiday of your dreams' = YAXSHI ta'til
'nightmare' = YOMON ta'til
→ B

A XATO: matnda NARX haqida gap yo'q.
C XATO: matnda TOZALIK haqida gap yo'q
(isitish, kalit, qo'ng'iroq bor).

exercises.instructionEn: Listen to the three short dialogues and decide who is: a) making a reservation at a restaurant; b) inviting somebody out; c) buying souvenirs. In pairs, act out the dialogues.
exercises.instructionUz: Uchta qisqa dialogni tinglang va kim: a) restoranda joy band qilayotganini; b) birovni taklif qilayotganini; c) sovg'a sotib olayotganini aniqlang. Juftlikda dialoglarni sahnalashtiring.
exercises.explanationUz:
DIQQAT — AUDIO ShART EMAS:
  Uchala dialog ham betda TO'LIQ bosilgan.


BARCHA JAVOBLAR:
  1-dialog  →  b) inviting somebody out
               (birovni taklif qilish)
  2-dialog  →  c) buying souvenirs
               (sovg'a sotib olish)
  3-dialog  →  a) making a reservation at a
               restaurant
               (restoranda joy band qilish)


1-DIALOG (TO'LIQ) — b) TAKLIF QILISh:

  A: Hello, Rachel. What are you doing
     tonight?
  B: I haven't got any plans. Why?
  A: Well, there's a good film on at the Odeon
     tonight. Would you like to go?
  B: Yes — that would be great!
  A: Okay. I'll pick you up at eight, then.

  Tarjimasi:
  A: Salom, Reychel. Bugun kechqurun nima
     qilyapsan?
  B: Hech qanday rejam yo'q. Nima edi?
  A: Bugun kechqurun Odeonda yaxshi kino bor.
     Borishni xohlaysanmi?
  B: Ha — zo'r bo'lardi!
  A: Yaxshi. Unda sakkizda kelib olib
     ketaman.

  KALIT: 'WOULD YOU LIKE TO GO?' — taklif.


2-DIALOG (TO'LIQ) — c) SOVG'A SOTIB OLISh:

  A: Can I help you?
  B: Yes, please. I'm looking for a gift to
     take home for my brother.
  A: How about this wallet? It's a lovely gift
     for a man.
  B: How much is it?
  A: It's only £10.
  B: Great — I'll take it. I'm sure he'll like
     it.

  Tarjimasi:
  A: Yordam bera olamanmi?
  B: Ha, iltimos. Akamga olib ketish uchun
     sovg'a qidiryapman.
  A: Bu hamyon qanday? Erkak uchun ajoyib
     sovg'a.
  B: Qancha turadi?
  A: Atigi 10 funt.
  B: Zo'r — olaman. Unga yoqishiga ishonchim
     komil.

  KALIT: 'I'm looking for a GIFT', 'How much
  is it?', 'I'LL TAKE IT' — do'kondagi savdo.


3-DIALOG (TO'LIQ) — a) JOY BAND QILISh:

  A: Hello. I'd like to book a table for
     tonight, please.
  B: Certainly, madam. What time and for how
     many?
  A: A table for two at nine o'clock, please.
  B: That's fine. Could I have your name,
     please?
  A: Powers. Ann Powers.
  B: Thank you, Ms Powers. We'll see you
     tonight.

  Tarjimasi:
  A: Salom. Bugun kechqurunga stol band
     qilmoqchi edim.
  B: Albatta, xonim. Soat nechada va necha
     kishiga?
  A: Soat to'qqizda ikki kishiga stol,
     iltimos.
  B: Yaxshi. Ismingizni ayta olasizmi?
  A: Pauers. Enn Pauers.
  B: Rahmat, Missis Pauers. Bugun kechqurun
     ko'rishguncha.

  KALIT: 'I'd like to BOOK A TABLE' —
  restoranda joy band qilish.


QANDAY ANIQLANADI — HAR DIALOGDA BITTA
KALIT IBORA:

  1  'Would you like to go?'   →  TAKLIF (b)
  2  'I'm looking for a gift'  →  XARID (c)
  3  'I'd like to book a table' → BAND QILISh (a)


HAR VAZIYAT UChUN FOYDALI IBORALAR:

  TAKLIF QILISh (inviting somebody out):
     'What are you doing tonight?'
     'Would you like to go?'
     'Yes, that would be great!'
     'I'll pick you up at eight.'

     RAD ETISh:
     'I'd love to, but I can't.'
     'Sorry, I'm busy tonight.'

  XARID QILISh (buying souvenirs):
     'Can I help you?'
     'I'm looking for ...'
     'How about this ...?'
     'How much is it?'
     'I'll take it.'

  JOY BAND QILISh (making a reservation):
     'I'd like to book a table.'
     'What time and for how many?'
     'A table for two at nine o'clock.'
     'Could I have your name, please?'


DIQQAT — 'I'LL TAKE IT':
  'I'LL take it' = olaman (sotib olaman)
  Do'konda qaror qabul qilish shakli.
  WILL — ayni damdagi qaror (Unit 13).


DIQQAT — 'TO PICK SOMEBODY UP':
  'I'll PICK YOU UP at eight.'
  = sakkizda kelib olib ketaman (mashinada)

  Ajraladigan fe'l:
     pick you up  ✓
     pick up you  ✗ (olmosh bilan faqat
                     o'rtada)


DIQQAT — 'MS':
  'Thank you, MS Powers.'
  Ms /mɪz/ — ayolga murojaat, turmush
  qurgan-qurmaganini bildirmaydi.

     Mrs — turmush qurgan ayol
     Miss — turmush qurmagan ayol
     Ms — ikkalasiga ham (zamonaviy, odobli)


DIQQAT — 'CERTAINLY, MADAM':
  Xizmat sohasida odobli murojaat:
     'madam' — ayolga
     'sir' — erkakka


DIQQAT — 'COULD I HAVE ...?':
  'COULD I have your name, please?'
  'could' — 'can' dan ODOBLIROQ
  (Grammar 60-bet).


YANGI SO'ZLAR:
  a reservation   = joy band qilish
  to book a table = stol band qilmoq
  to invite somebody out = birovni taklif
                    qilmoq
  plans           = rejalar
  the Odeon       = Odeon (kinoteatr nomi)
  to pick somebody up = kelib olib ketmoq
  a gift          = sovg'a
  a wallet        = hamyon (erkak)
  How much is it? = Qancha turadi?
  Certainly       = Albatta
  madam / sir     = xonim / janob
  Ms              = ayolga murojaat

pairs.left: 1-dialog: 'Hello, Rachel. What are you doing tonight? ... Would you like to go?'
pairs.leftUz: 'Salom, Reychel. Bugun kechqurun nima qilyapsan? ... Borishni xohlaysanmi?'
pairs.whyUz:
KALIT: 'WOULD YOU LIKE TO GO?' — taklif
qilish shakli.

Yana: 'there's a good film ON at the Odeon' —
kinoga taklif.
'I'll PICK YOU UP at eight' — kelib olib
ketish (uchrashuv kelishilgan).

Bu — restoranda joy band qilish ham,
xarid ham emas.

pairs.left: 2-dialog: 'Can I help you? ... I'm looking for a gift to take home for my brother.'
pairs.whyUz:
UCH KALIT:
  'I'm looking for a GIFT'
  'HOW MUCH IS IT?'
  'I'LL TAKE IT'

Bu — do'kondagi savdo suhbati.
'a wallet' = hamyon.
'£10' — funt sterling.

'I'LL take it' — do'konda sotib olish qarori
(WILL — ayni damdagi qaror).

pairs.left: 3-dialog: 'Hello. I'd like to book a table for tonight, please.'
pairs.right: a) making a reservation at a restaurant
pairs.leftUz: 'Salom. Bugun kechqurunga stol band qilmoqchi edim.'
pairs.whyUz:
KALIT: 'I'd like to BOOK A TABLE' — birinchi
gapdayoq aniq.

Yana: 'What time and FOR HOW MANY?' —
necha kishiga.
'A table FOR TWO at nine o'clock.'
'Could I have your NAME?' — band qilishda
ism so'raladi.

107-bet, 14-mashqda ham 'book a table' bor
edi.

items.base: I'd like to book a table

patterns.exampleEn: Tip your bellboy generously, and you'll have the perfect holiday. Don't tip him, and you'll have the worst holiday of your life!
patterns.exampleUz: Xizmatchiga saxiylik bilan choychaqa bering — mukammal ta'til o'tkazasiz. Bermang — eng yomon ta'til bo'ladi!
patterns.explanationUz:
Bu yerda 'AND' = 'shunda'.
Unit 14 dagi 'OR' = 'aks holda' ning
teskarisi.

patterns.exampleEn: Guests who don't tip well often find that ... Anyone who is planning to stay in an American hotel should remember ...
patterns.exampleUz: Yaxshi choychaqa bermaydigan mehmonlar ko'pincha sezishadi ... Amerika mehmonxonasida turishni rejalashtirayotgan har kim esda tutsin ...
patterns.explanationUz:
'WHO' — ODAMLAR uchun ergash gap
bog'lovchisi ('which' — narsalar uchun).

patterns.exampleEn: Americans take tipping more seriously than any other nationality. No one takes tipping as seriously as hotel bellboys do.
patterns.exampleUz: Amerikaliklar choychaqa berishga har qanday millatdan jiddiyroq qaraydi. Hech kim xizmatchilardek jiddiy qaramaydi.

patterns.formula: WOULD YOU LIKE TO + [fe'l] ?  —  Yes, that would be great!
patterns.exampleEn: There's a good film on at the Odeon tonight. Would you like to go? — Yes, that would be great!
patterns.exampleUz: Bugun Odeonda yaxshi kino bor. Borishni xohlaysanmi? — Ha, zo'r bo'lardi!
patterns.explanationUz:
TAKLIF qilish shakli.
Rad etish: 'I'd love to, but I can't.'

patterns.formula: I'M LOOKING FOR + [narsa].  —  How much is it?  —  I'LL TAKE IT.
patterns.exampleEn: I'm looking for a gift for my brother. — How much is it? — It's only £10. — I'll take it.
patterns.exampleUz: Akamga sovg'a qidiryapman. — Qancha turadi? — Atigi 10 funt. — Olaman.
patterns.explanationUz:
Do'kondagi savdo suhbati.
'I'LL take it' — ayni damdagi qaror (WILL).

patterns.formula: I'D LIKE TO BOOK A TABLE FOR + [vaqt/kishi soni].
patterns.exampleEn: I'd like to book a table for tonight. — A table for two at nine o'clock, please.
patterns.exampleUz: Bugun kechqurunga stol band qilmoqchi edim. — Soat to'qqizda ikki kishiga stol, iltimos.
patterns.explanationUz:
Restoranda joy band qilish shakli.
'a table FOR two' — necha kishiga.
